content: I'll read the test image to analyze the plant disease symptoms.

**Visual Analysis:**

- **Plant type/part affected:** Cauliflower head (curd)
- **Color:** The curd has turned yellow-green (instead of normal creamy white), with brownish patches — particularly in the lower portion
- **Texture/pattern:** The curd surface shows softening and irregular decay areas; sections appear water-soaked and mushy, with brown discoloration spreading across multiple florets
- **No distinct V-shaped lesions, concentric target rings, or powdery/downy fungal growth visible**

**Reasoning through the classes:**

- **Alternaria Leaf Spot** — Causes concentric, target-board circular lesions with yellow halos, primarily on leaves. No such pattern visible here.
- **Downy Mildew** — Causes pale yellow spots on upper leaf surface with grayish-purple downy growth underneath; on cauliflower curds, produces small discrete dark "pepper spots." Not what I see here.
- **Black Rot** — Bacterial disease (Xanthomonas) causing V-shaped yellow-brown lesions at leaf margins with vascular blackening. The symptoms here are diffuse and not V-shaped.
- **Bacterial Soft Rot** — Caused by Pectobacterium/Erwinia species. Produces soft, water-soaked, mushy tissue that turns brownish and decays; frequently affects cauliflower heads causing yellowing and soft brown decay of the curd. This matches the yellowing curd with brown soft patches seen in the image.

The soft, mushy browning of the cauliflower curd with diffuse yellowing is characteristic of **Bacterial Soft Rot**.
